items.title: Graham Breaks With Trump Over Russia Sanctions Law Her Brother Championed
items.author: Michael Gold
items.content: <article>Senator Darline Graham, appointed to fill the Senate seat of her late brother, Lindsey, gently disagreed with the president’s decision to exempt Russia from the sanctions legislation.</article>

items.title: In Midterm Campaign’s Final Stretch, Trump Can’t Stop Praising Men’s Bodies
items.author: Tim Balk
items.content: <article>As he stumps for midterm candidates, the president has been especially eager to talk about the physical appearance of some men.</article>

items.title: Israel Must Probe West Bank Attack on Journalist, US Envoy Says
items.author: María Paula Mijares Torres
items.content: <article>US Ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee condemned the beating of a Washington Post journalist while working in the West Bank and demanded a “full investigation, arrest and prosecution” of the attackers.</article>

items.title: Bernie Sanders Visits Florida to Campaign With Angie Nixon
items.author: Patricia Mazzei
items.content: <article>Senator Bernie Sanders of Vermont has made a point of investing in Republican-leaning states. He rallied in Tampa for Ms. Nixon, the underdog Democratic nominee for Florida Senate.</article>

items.title: Guatemalan Former Anti-Corruption Prosecutor Killed in Capital
items.author: Mie Dahl
items.content: <article>Former Guatemalan anti-corruption prosecutor Juan Francisco Solórzano Foppa was shot dead in Guatemala City, reviving concern over the safety of the justice officials who take on powerful political and criminal interests in the country.</article>

items.title: Susan Collins Criticizes Rival’s ‘Oh, Shut Up’ Comment as ‘Very Telling’
items.author: Tim Balk and Eoin Higgins
items.content: <article>Ms. Collins, a Republican running in a crucial race, said the debate remark by Troy Jackson reflected how he treated women. Mr. Jackson defended his comment.</article>

items.title: Ex-South African President Jacob Zuma Discharged from Hospital
items.author: Mike Cohen
items.content: <article>Former South African President Jacob Zuma has been discharged from the hospital after undergoing “a routine medical checkup,” his party said.</article>

items.title: Dispute Between Trump Allies Centers on Millions Transferred From Congo
items.author: Tyler Pager and Anatoly Kurmanaev
items.content: <article>The White House inquiry is focused on diverging accounts from Richard Grenell and Alina Habba Mildon about a $17 million transfer from a government account in the African country to a Texas defense firm.</article>

items.title: Albania Protesters Clash With Police as Premier Faces Pressure
items.author: Gresa Kraja
items.content: <article>Albanian police clashed with hundreds of protesters in the capital, using tear gas and water cannons to disperse crowds demanding Prime Minister Edi Rama’s resignation for a fifth consecutive day.</article>

items.title: Trump’s Russia Sanctions Waiver Called Mistake by GOP Allies
items.author: María Paula Mijares Torres and Jeff Mason
items.content: <article>Republican lawmakers blasted Donald Trump for waiving new tariffs and sanctions on Russia, prompting the president to defend himself against members of his own party.</article>

items.title: Romania Shoots Down Two Drones Over Its Black Sea Waters
items.author: Irina Vilcu
items.content: <article>Romania said it shot down two drones over its territorial waters on Saturday, the latest incident as Russia intensifies attacks on Ukraine’s shipping route in the Black Sea.</article>

items.title: Ilhan Omar’s Sister’s Phone Was Seized Before Search of Lawmaker’s Home
items.author: Ernesto Londoño, Alan Feuer and Hamed Aleaziz
items.content: <article>A criminal investigation into the lawmaker’s immigration process advanced after federal investigators reviewed family text messages from a seized phone.</article>

items.title: U.S. Floats Lifeline to Russia: Allowing More Gas Sales to Europe
items.author: Anton Troianovski and Jim Tankersley
items.content: <article>The Trump administration is pitching the idea as part of a peace deal with Ukraine, but Europe is wary and critics say Russia would be strengthened.</article>

items.title: White House Turmoil Erupts as Trump Axes Zacharia, Backs Wiles
items.author: Josh Wingrove and Hadriana Lowenkron
items.content: <article>Infighting gripping Donald Trump’s White House spilled into public view this week, with the abrupt exit of his hand-picked press secretary and the president forced to quash swirling questions about his chief of staff’s future.</article>

items.title: Scottish Nationalists Try to Get Independence Back on UK Agenda
items.author: Alastair Reed
items.content: <article>Scottish First Minister John Swinney intensified his push for a second referendum on independence, countering Prime Minister Andy Burnham’s offer to work together and design a new model of regional empowerment.</article>

items.title: Hungary to Unveil 2027 Budget Monday, Laying Out Euro Road Map
items.author: Thomas Escritt
items.content: <article>Hungary’s Prime Minister Peter Magyar said he would present the country’s 2027 budget in a speech to parliament at 1pm on Monday.</article>

items.title: Opposition Retains Czech Senate Control as Premier’s Party Slips
items.author: Michal Kubala
items.content: <article>Control of the Czech Senate will remain in the hands of the current opposition after Prime Minister Andrej Babis’s ANO party lost ground in the upper house.</article>

items.title: What Pennsylvania Reveals About the Midterms
items.author: Shane Goldmacher, Alexandra Ostasiewicz, Joy Sung, Nour Idriss, June Kim and Edward Vega
items.content: <article>In Pennsylvania, four congressional districts exemplify the types of seats that Democrats are aiming to flip. Our national political correspondent Shane Goldmacher explains.</article>

items.title: Trump Signs Order Waiving New Russia Sanctions
items.author: Alan Rappeport
items.content: <article>The sanctions were part of a measure that was named after Senator Lindsey Graham, the South Carolina Republican who died in July.</article>

items.title: Republicans Brace For Backlash as Trump Gas Prices Near Biden’s
items.author: Kevin Crowley
items.content: <article>In his 2024 presidential campaign, Donald Trump made the cost of energy a centerpiece.</article>

items.title: Trump Revives 2020 Election Conspiracy Theories as Midterms Loom
items.author: Richard Fausset
items.content: <article>Voting rights advocates fear the Trump administration may use the federal government to cast doubt on the election, discourage participation or try to delegitimize results.</article>

items.title: How Pennsylvania Explains the Forces Shaping the Midterms
items.author: Shane Goldmacher
items.content: <article>Four battleground congressional districts in the state reveal fault lines that are echoing nationwide.</article>

items.title: Egypt Ready to Defend Saudi Arabia if Needed, Sisi Says
items.author: Tarek El-Tablawy
items.content: <article>Egyptian President Abdel-Fattah El-Sisi said his nation stands ready to defend Saudi Arabia as it comes under attack from Yemen’s Houthis and called on parliament to convene an emergency session to authorize such action if it became necessary.</article>

items.title: SpaceX Starlink Cuts Hobbled Ukraine Before Russian Bombardment
items.author: Ellen Milligan and Tony Capaccio
items.content: <article>Restrictions on Ukraine’s use of SpaceX’s satellite technology came just weeks after its forces relied on the network for a surprising and successful counter-offensive that retook critical territory from Russian forces.</article>

items.title: Houthis Hit Yemen Airport as Saudi Arabia Intercepts Attacks
items.author: Sara Gharaibeh
items.content: <article>Yemen’s Houthis struck the main airport in the nation’s interim capital on Friday, while its missiles and drones fired toward Saudi Arabia were intercepted, as the flare-up in fighting showed no sign of abating.</article>

items.title: Burnham Finds His Plans to Focus on Britain Blown Up by Trump
items.author: Alex Wickham and Chloe Chaplain
items.content: <article>Prime Minister Andy Burnham’s bid to break from Keir Starmer’s premiership by focusing more on UK domestic policy and less on global events is proving near impossible in Donald Trump’s world.</article>

items.title: Justice Department Seeks to Disqualify Judge Overseeing Golf Course Lawsuit
items.author: Zach Montague
items.content: <article>Escalating a standoff with Judge Ana C. Reyes, the Justice Department demanded that she recuse herself from a case in which she had ordered several Trump officials to testify.</article>

items.title: Katie Zacharia, Trump’s New Press Secretary, Is Ousted After 5 Days
items.author: Shawn McCreesh, Tyler Pager and Hamed Aleaziz
items.content: <article>Her abrupt departure came after she was shadowed by questions about how she had presented her legal career and handled her first press briefing.</article>

items.title: Congressional Staff Open Letters Containing Suspicious Substances
items.author: Chris Cameron
items.content: <article>The incidents, the first of which was reported on Thursday, came as election officials have reported a growing number of threats directed at them.</article>

items.title: Appeals Court Questions Justice Dept. Claim That Trump Owns White House Records
items.author: Zach Montague
items.content: <article>A three-judge panel appeared unconvinced by claims that a federal law requiring the president to preserve and hand over his presidential papers was unconstitutional.</article>

items.title: Trump Halts New Russia Energy Sanctions to Ease Diesel Costs
items.author: Alicia Diaz
items.content: <article>President Donald Trump waived massive tariffs linked to Russian energy exports mandated in a law that he signed last month, as the measures complicated his push to lower diesel prices ahead of the US midterm elections.</article>

items.title: RFK Jr. Pledged to Advance Anti-Vaccine Group’s Goals. Here’s What He’s Doing.
items.author: Christina Jewett
items.content: <article>The health secretary is quietly taking steps that public health experts fear will reduce immunization rates further.</article>

items.title: Trump Administration Restricts Drone Activity Along U.S.-Mexico Border
items.author: Karoun Demirjian
items.content: <article>The new restrictions ban unauthorized drone flights within a nautical mile of the southern border, up to 400 feet in the air.</article>

items.title: N.I.H. Hospital Board Rebukes Kennedy Over New Vaccine Injury Clinic
items.author: Sheryl Gay Stolberg
items.content: <article>The board that oversees the N.I.H. Clinical Center voted unanimously to support a statement accusing Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. of undermining trust in the hospital’s work.</article>

items.title: Trump Returns to Dalton for a Rescue Mission in Georgia
items.author: Jess Bidgood
items.content: <article>Plus, Katie Zacharia’s ouster, A.O.C. on the trail, and another tense debate in Maine.</article>

items.title: Alberta Separation Referendum Draws Over 1 Million Early Votes in Canada
items.author: Iain Boekhoff and Derek Decloet
items.content: <article>More than 1 million people have already cast their ballots in Alberta’s referendum on separation from Canada, signaling strong voter turnout that pollsters say may favor the “remain” side.</article>

items.title: Russia Appears to Step Up Efforts to Influence U.S. Voters
items.author: Julian E. Barnes, Dustin Volz and Steven Lee Myers
items.content: <article>One campaign has created social media posts focusing on U.S. support for Israel to sow discord ahead of the midterm elections.</article>

items.title: Trump’s New White House Press Secretary Out After Five Days
items.author: Josh Wingrove, Hadriana Lowenkron and Skylar Woodhouse
items.content: <article>Katie Zacharia will no longer serve as President Donald Trump’s press secretary after spending less than a week on the job, thrusting the White House’s communications operation back into a state of chaos.</article>
